meta.title: Lídia Belas — Researcher · Digital Anthropology, Gender and Digital Cultures
meta.description: Lídia Belas — undergraduate student in Social Sciences/UFBA, PIBIC scholarship holder at LABHDUFBA. Research online misogyny, digital games, gender and technology.
hero.subtitle: Researcher in training · Digital Humanities · UFBA
hero.research: Online misogyny in digital games and player communities, from an anthropological approach.
about.label: About me
about.p1: I am an undergraduate student in Social Sciences — Anthropology at the Faculty of Philosophy and Human Sciences (FFCH) of the Federal University of Bahia (UFBA). My interest in the Humanities, however, began before university. I grew up in a family of teachers in the area and, especially from high school, I realized that it was in this field that I wanted to build my trajectory.
about.p2: An especially important experience in this path was my time at the Federal Institute of Education, Science and Technology of Bahia (IFBA), Simões Filho campus, where I attended high school integrated with the technical course in Metallurgy. I completed high school, but not the technical course, due to the interruptions caused by the Covid-19 pandemic. Still, I consider the period at IFBA a fundamental part of my training, both for the experiences and for the people and relationships I have
about.p3: My current interest in games and digital cultures is also born from a personal experience. League of Legends game since 2020, and my experience as a woman in a competitive gaming environment was marked by different situations of hostility and the recurring perception that that space did not always recognize me as someone who should be there. These experiences helped transform an everyday experience into a research question.
about.p4: It is from these experiences that I have been building questions about gender, technology, sociability, belonging and conflict in digital environments, especially in games and player communities.
research.label: Research agenda
research.focus: My main focus currently is online misogyny in games and player communities, investigated from an anthropological approach that articulates research in digital environments and corpus exploration.
